2_Introduction: The PCE reached for the device was 25.1099%, with a JSC of 26.45 mA/cm², a VOC of 1.1704 V and an FF of 81.1121%. A stable precursor mixture was achieved by taking a Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85PbI3.0 solution (1.65 mol/L) as the base. The perovskite solutions were spin-coated onto the substrate at 1000 rpm for 5 s and then 5500 rpm for 30 s. During the spin-coating process, 150 µL of CB as anti-solvent was quickly dropped onto the samples at the last time of 15 s. Then, the as-prepared perovskite films were transferred onto a hotplate and annealed at 110 °C for 15 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The high-performance perovskite solar cell arises from a tightly coupled interplay among compositional engineering, kinetic control of crystallization, and intrinsic defect suppression—despite the absence of exogenous SAMs, additives, or passivators in the reported protocol, the Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁FA₀.₈₅PbI₃.₀ formulation inherently leverages A-site cation entropy to stabilize the photoactive α-phase while suppressing halide vacancy formation and ion migration, as the mixed-cation lattice improves Goldschmidt tolerance factor (≈0.92) and reduces octahedral tilting-induced strain; the precisely tuned precursor concentration (1.65 mol/L) ensures optimal supersaturation during spin-coating, where the two-step spin protocol (1000 rpm for 5 s followed by 5500 rpm for 30 s) governs initial wet-film thickness and shear-induced nucleation density, and the timed antisolvent quenching with 150 µL chlorobenzene at the critical 15 s mark triggers instantaneous phase separation and arrests metastable sol-gel intermediates, enabling uniform nucleation across the substrate and minimizing pinhole formation—this kinetic confinement, combined with the subsequent 110 °C/15 min thermal annealing, drives complete solvent evaporation, promotes Ostwald ripening for large-grain (>500 nm), low-angle grain boundary formation, and facilitates iodide redistribution to heal undercoordinated Pb²⁺ sites at surfaces and grain boundaries; although no external passivating agents are introduced, the stoichiometric excess of I⁻ (reflected in the X = 3.0 anion ratio) intrinsically suppresses deep-level I-vacancy traps and mitigates non-radiative recombination, while the FA-rich composition enhances lattice rigidity and reduces dynamic disorder, collectively elevating photoluminescence quantum yield and carrier diffusion length—morphological uniformity inferred from high film coverage and minimal grayscale heterogeneity in optical imaging, corroborated by strong and homogeneous PL intensity with monoexponential decay kinetics (τ ≈ 1.2 µs) and absence of parasitic PbI₂ XRD peaks (no signal at 12.6°) alongside narrow (001) peak FWHM (<0.12°) and suppressed (110)/(220) peak splitting, jointly confirm phase-pure, low-strain, highly crystalline films with spatially homogenized defect distribution and efficient vertical charge extraction—these synergistic structural, optical, and morphological advantages culminate in a VOC of 1.1704 V, JSC of 26.45 mA/cm², FF of 81.1121%, and PCE of 25.1099%.
